mainTopic: Joining separate witnesses under 'דבר ולא חצי דבר', and a thief who sells the stolen animal on שבת
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא. A person ate a field's produce for three years, with a different pair of witnesses seeing each year. One תנא says this counts as a חזקה. The other agrees, but notes that רבי עקיבא disagrees, because testimony must be 'a whole matter, not half a matter'. אביי answers that our משנה can still fit רבי עקיבא. When one pair of witnesses proves something by itself, like עדי קידושין or עדי גניבה, the other pair may build on it. The גמרא then asks what the word 'דבר' excludes for the רבנן, and settles on two pairs who each saw only one hair on a girl. Next the גמרא asks why our משנה makes a thief who sold on שבת pay, while a ברייתא exempts him. רמי בר חמא and רב פפא each explain the ברייתא as a sale made through a שבת act punished by death. רבא then defends רמי בר חמא with the case of אתנן, and his argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three years eaten, each in front of a different pair of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether three separate pairs of witnesses, one pair for each year, can together establish a three-year חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: (אבא) חלפתא, he said to him: What if a person ate the field's produce the first year in front of two witnesses, the second year in front of two other witnesses, and the third year in front of two more witnesses? What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא records a question about a person who wants to prove ownership of a field by showing he ate its produce for three years. Each year was seen by a different pair of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A three-year חזקה normally needs testimony covering all three years. The question is whether three separate partial testimonies can be added together, even though no single pair saw the full three years.

keyTerms.meaning: He ate it, meaning he harvested and used the field's produce as an owner
In front of two witnesses
What is the law?

phrases.english: Ḥalafta, he said to him:
phrases.notes: This finishes the opening of a ברייתא that started just before. The two people talking are אבא חלפתא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁאֲכָלָהּ שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: If he ate it the first year in front of two,
the second in front of two,
the third in front of two, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי שֶׁאֲכָלָהּ שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting to show whose view our משנה follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can three separate pairs of witnesses, each covering one year, combine to establish a three-year חזקה?

steps.title: Yes, it counts as a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The other תנא answers that the separate testimonies do combine, so this is a valid חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The question gets a clear answer: the three pairs together are enough to prove the three years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer treats each pair's testimony as one valid piece of a larger picture. The pieces can be added up even though no pair saw everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Proof of ownership through three years of using the property openly
This is, this counts as

phrases.english: He said to him: This is a presumption of ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הֲרֵי זוֹ חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three separate testimonies combine and establish a חזקה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא disagrees: a whole matter, not half a matter
steps.stepSummary: The questioner agrees but reports that רבי עקיבא disputes it, because witnesses must testify to a complete matter, not part of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I also say so. But רבי עקיבא disagrees on this, because רבי עקיבא used to say: The Torah says 'a matter', and that means a whole matter, not half a matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The first speaker agrees with the answer, but adds that רבי עקיבא holds differently. This is the reason the גמרא brought the ברייתא: to show that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, each pair here testifies to only one year, which is just a piece of the three-year חזקה. A piece is 'half a matter', so it does not count, and the pieces cannot be joined. Our משנה seems to combine separate pairs of witnesses, so it looks like it disagrees with רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Disagrees on this matter
A whole matter and not half a matter. Testimony must prove a complete case.

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the main obstacle the rest of the סוגיא has to deal with: can our משנה, which joins separate testimonies, fit רבי עקיבא's view?
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not say the witnesses are lying. He says each pair proves only part of what needs proving, and partial testimony does not count.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כֵּן,
phrases.english: He said to him: I too say so,
but Rabbi Akiva disagrees on the matter.
For Rabbi Akiva used to say:
"A matter": and not half a matter.
phrases.notes: The word 'דבר' comes from the פסוק about witnesses, דברים 19:15.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא חוֹלֵק בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with step 2 but adds רבי עקיבא's opposing view, which is the point the גמרא needs from this ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, witnesses must testify to a complete matter. Separate partial testimonies do not combine.

steps.title: אביי: even רבי עקיבא could agree with our משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the claim that our משנה goes against רבי עקיבא. He points to a case where רבי עקיבא would accept one pair's testimony even though it depends on another pair's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say our משנה follows רבי עקיבא. Doesn't רבי עקיבא agree in a case where two witnesses say 'he betrothed her' and two other witnesses say 'someone had relations with her'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against the conclusion from the ברייתא. He argues that our משנה can fit רבי עקיבא too, and starts to prove it from a case רבי עקיבא would surely accept. The next two steps finish his argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the betrothal case, the second pair's testimony (relations) is a sin of adultery only because of the first pair's testimony (קידושין). Even so, everyone, רבי עקיבא included, accepts the second pair's testimony as complete. אביי will use this to show that a testimony which builds on another pair's testimony is not 'half a matter'. So the case in our משנה is different from the three-year חזקה case.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. Used to show a source can fit a view that seemed to be ruled out.
Doesn't he agree? A rhetorical question that brings a case everyone accepts
He betrothed her, making her an אשת איש
He had relations with her

steps.confusionAlert: The difference from the three-year חזקה case is not that each pair saw a different event. There too, each pair saw a different year. The difference is that the עדי קידושין prove something legally meaningful all by themselves, as the next step explains.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא –
phrases.english: Abaye said: You can even say it follows Rabbi Akiva:
phrases.notes: 'It' is our משנה, which the גמרא just said was not like רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: doesn't Rabbi Akiva agree
in a case where two say "he betrothed her"
and two say "someone had relations with her,"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion drawn from step 3 that our משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that our משנה goes against רבי עקיבא. It does not reject רבי עקיבא's rule of 'דבר ולא חצי דבר' itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not every testimony that depends on another pair is 'half a matter'. רבי עקיבא himself accepts the second pair in the קידושין and relations case.

steps.title: Why the betrothal and intercourse witnesses each count as a full matter
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains his case. The עדי ביאה depend on the עדי קידושין, but the עדי קידושין do not depend on them. So each pair's testimony counts as a full 'דבר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the witnesses about the intercourse need the witnesses about the betrothal, the betrothal witnesses do not need the intercourse witnesses. So don't we call this a full 'matter'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is finishing the case he just raised. He explains why even רבי עקיבא would accept the second pair of עדים there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עדי ביאה mean nothing unless we already know the woman was betrothed. But the עדי קידושין prove something real all by themselves. Since one side stands alone, רבי עקיבא calls the whole thing a full 'דבר', even though the other side leans on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who testify that the woman had relations
Witnesses who testify that the woman was betrothed
They need (they depend on)
We call it / we read the word as applying to it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that any dependence on another pair makes testimony 'half a matter'. It is 'half a matter' only when neither pair proves anything alone. Here only the עדי ביאה depend on the others, so רבי עקיבא accepts it.

phrases.english: For even though
the witnesses of the intercourse need the witnesses of the betrothal

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּעֵדֵי קִדּוּשִׁין לָא צְרִיכִי לְעֵדֵי בִיאָה,
phrases.english: since the witnesses of the betrothal do not need the witnesses of the intercourse,
do we not call it a 'matter'?
phrases.notes: This is the word 'דבר' from דברים 19:15, the source רבי עקיבא used for 'a full matter, not half'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּעֵדֵי בִיאָה צְרִיכִי לְעֵדֵי קִדּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning of the case אביי brought in Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that our משנה must go against רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The claim assumed that any testimony depending on another pair is 'half a matter'. But when one pair stands alone, רבי עקיבא counts both as a full matter.

steps.title: Applying the same logic to the theft and slaughter witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The עדי טביחה depend on the עדי גניבה, but the עדי גניבה stand alone. So here too each pair counts as a full 'דבר', and our משנה fits רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, even though the slaughter witnesses need the theft witnesses, the theft witnesses do not need the slaughter witnesses. So we call it a full 'matter'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the rule from the betrothal case and applies it to our משנה about a thief who steals and then slaughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony about slaughter means nothing unless the animal was stolen. But testimony about the theft already makes the person liable as a thief all by itself. Because the theft witnesses stand alone, this matches the betrothal case, and רבי עקיבא would agree with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too (the same logic applies)
Slaughtering (the stolen animal)
Theft

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, testimony is 'half a matter' only when neither side stands on its own. If one pair proves something by itself, the other pair can build on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that our משנה does not have to be explained as going against רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Here too,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּעֵדֵי טְבִיחָה צְרִיכִי לְעֵדֵי גְנֵיבָה –
phrases.english: even though the witnesses of the slaughter need the witnesses of the theft

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּעֵדֵי גְנֵיבָה לָא צְרִיכִי לְעֵדֵי טְבִיחָה,
phrases.english: since the witnesses of the theft do not need the witnesses of the slaughter,
we call it a 'matter'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning from Step 5 to the case in our משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה works even according to רבי עקיבא, because the theft witnesses stand on their own.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from the word 'matter'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן disagree with רבי עקיבא, but they too have the word 'דבר' in the פסוק. The גמרא asks what that word comes to exclude for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: this 'a matter and not half a matter', what does it come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן, who argue with רבי עקיבא. It asks what they do with the same word 'דבר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do accept split testimony from separate pairs. So the word 'דבר' must teach them some other case that is excluded. The גמרא wants to know which case.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי עקיבא
Half a matter (testimony that proves only part of what is needed)
To exclude what?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis –
this 'a matter and not half a matter',
comes to exclude what?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן הַאי דָּבָר וְלֹא חֲצִי דָבָר לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רבי עקיבא's view, the גמרא asks how the opposing רבנן use the same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case the word 'דבר' excludes according to the רבנן.

steps.title: It excludes two witnesses who each saw one hair
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן, 'דבר' excludes this case: one witness says he saw one hair on the girl's back, and another says he saw one hair on her belly.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude a case where one witness says he saw one hair on her back, and one says he saw one hair on her belly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. For the רבנן, the word 'דבר' rules out combining two single witnesses who each saw only one sign of adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl counts as grown up only with two hairs. Each witness here proves only one, so neither testimony shows anything by itself. The רבנן say these two testimonies do not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness says
Her back
Her belly

phrases.english: To exclude where one says he saw one hair on her back,
phrases.notes: A girl counts as grown up when she has two hairs, so each witness here proves only half of that.

phrases.english: and one says he saw one hair on her belly.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי אֶחָד אוֹמֵר אֶחָד בְּגַבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'דבר' excludes two single witnesses who each saw one hair.

steps.title: That case is obvious, since it is also half a testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a verse is not needed for this case. Each witness gives only half a matter, and each one alone is only half a testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is half a matter and also half a testimony!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 8. That case would fail anyway, so the word 'דבר' cannot be needed to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every testimony needs two עדים. In the hair case each fact is told by only one witness, so it is 'half a testimony' as well as 'half a matter'. It is obviously invalid without any special word from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a testimony (only one witness instead of two)
This (case)

phrases.english: This is half a matter
and half a testimony!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי חֲצִי דָבָר וַחֲצִי עֵדוּת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'דבר' is needed to exclude the case of one hair per witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case already fails because each fact has only one witness. So the word 'דבר' would teach nothing new there.

steps.title: A new answer: 'דבר' excludes two pairs who each saw one hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier answer. For the רבנן, 'דבר' excludes a case where one pair of witnesses saw one hair on the girl's back and another pair saw one hair on her belly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to exclude: two say one hair on her back, and two say one hair on her belly. These say she is a minor, and those say she is a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier answer was knocked down in step 9, so the גמרא gives a new case that the word 'דבר' comes to exclude for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each side is a full pair of witnesses, so each one is a complete set of עדים. But each pair saw only one hair, and one hair alone does not show the girl is grown up. So each pair is really saying 'she is still a קטנה', and we need the פסוק to teach that we cannot join the two pairs together.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude; what the word comes to leave out
on her back
on her belly
a minor girl, not yet grown up

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, 'דבר' teaches that two pairs of witnesses who each give only half a matter cannot be joined into one full testimony.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to exclude
two say one hair on her back,
and two say one hair on her belly –
these are saying she is a minor,
and those are saying she is a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַעוֹטֵי שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים אֶחָד בְּגַבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 9 rejected with a new case that really needs a פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word 'דבר' exclude according to the רבנן?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two pairs of witnesses, each pair testifying to only one hair in a different place, cannot be joined together.

steps.title: Our משנה says stealing and selling on שבת is liable, but a ברייתא says exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a thief who sold on שבת pays four or five times, and points out that a ברייתא says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He stole and sold on שבת, etc. But it was taught in a ברייתא: he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and right away sets a ברייתא against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה holds the thief liable for the four or five payment even though he sold on שבת. A ברייתא says the same case is exempt. Both cannot be true as they stand, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.english: He stole and sold on Shabbat [etc.].
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which says he still pays four or five times.

phrases.english: But it was taught: he is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a thief who sold on שבת pays four or five times.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules the opposite in what looks like the same case.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: the ברייתא means a sale done by picking a fig on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says the ברייתא that exempts is talking about a special case: the buyer told the thief to pick a fig from his tree on שבת, and by that act the buyer acquires the stolen animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: When that ברייתא taught that he is exempt, it is where the buyer says to him: 'Pick yourself a fig from my fig tree, and through that let your stolen animal become mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers the contradiction by putting the ברייתא in a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's case, the act that makes the sale happen is itself a שבת sin punished by death. So the thief is exempt from the money payment. In the משנה's case, the sale was done some other way, so he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: pick off, pluck
a fig; also a fig tree
and let it be acquired by me
your stolen item (the stolen animal)

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
When that baraita teaches that he is exempt –
it is where the buyer says to him:
"Pick yourself a fig from my fig tree,
phrases.notes: Picking from a tree on שבת is a sin punished by death, and when one act brings death and money together, he does not pay the money.

phrases.english: and through that let your stolen animal become mine."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא דְּפָטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the ברייתא is about a special way of selling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to rule differently on the very same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא exempts only when the sale itself was done through a שבת act punished by death.

steps.title: If the court would not enforce it, it is not a real sale
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים attack רמי בר חמא's answer: if the buyer came to court, we would not make the thief hand over the animal, since he is liable to death. So that sale is not a sale at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: But since, if the buyer claimed it from him before us in court, we would not tell him 'Go pay', because he is liable with his life, then the sale also is not a sale!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רמי בר חמא's answer from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the thief is liable to death for that act, the court would never force him to give the animal to the buyer. A sale that cannot be enforced is not a real sale. Without a real sale there is nothing to pay four or five times for, so the ברייתא would not call this 'selling' at all.

keyTerms.meaning: claimed, sued
go pay
liable with his life (death penalty)
a sale

phrases.english: They said:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּכִי תָבַע לֵיהּ קַמַּן בְּדִינָא
phrases.english: But since, if the buyer claims it from him before us in court,
we do not say to him: "Go pay" –
phrases.notes: He means: go hand over the animal you sold.

phrases.english: because he is liable with his life;

phrases.aramaic: הָא מְכִירָה נָמֵי לָאו מְכִירָה הִיא!
phrases.english: then the sale too is not a sale!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: וְכֵיוָן דְּכִי תָבַע לֵיהּ קַמַּן בְּדִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רמי בר חמא's answer from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's claim that the ברייתא is about a sale made through picking a fig on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sale the court would never enforce, because the seller is liable to death, is not a real sale. So the ברייתא could not be calling it a sale.

steps.title: רב פפא: The thief throws the animal into the buyer's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer: the ברייתא that exempts is talking about a buyer who told the thief to throw the stolen animal into his courtyard and acquire it that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: The ברייתא is talking about a buyer who says to the thief, 'Throw your stolen animal into my courtyard, and your stolen animal will be acquired by me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא's fig case was knocked down, so רב פפא offers a different case. Here the sale itself is the act that breaks שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the fig case, picking the fig did not make a real sale, because a sale tied to a death-penalty act cannot be enforced. רב פפא picks a case where the transfer of the animal and the שבת violation are one and the same act. When the thief throws the animal from the public domain into a private courtyard, he is carrying on שבת, a capital sin. Since the sale happens at the very same moment, the rule of קים ליה בדרבה מיניה exempts him from paying four or five times.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
Throw
Your stolen item (here, the stolen animal)
My courtyard. A person can acquire things that come into his own courtyard (קנין חצר).
It will be acquired by me

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רמי בר חמא's case. There, the שבת act (picking a fig) was a separate act from the animal itself. Here, throwing the animal is both the שבת violation and the sale.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
It is where the buyer says to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the thief. רב פפא is explaining the ברייתא that exempts the thief.

phrases.english: "Throw your stolen animal into my courtyard,
and your stolen animal will be acquired by me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רמי בר חמא's answer, which was rejected in Step 13, with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא could be the fig case, where the buyer acquires through the thief picking a fig on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is a case where throwing the animal into the buyer's courtyard is both the sale and a capital שבת violation, so the thief is exempt from paying four or five times.

steps.title: Whose view is this? רבי עקיבא's rule that an object in the air counts as resting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion רב פפא's case follows, and answers that it follows רבי עקיבא, who says an object in the air over an area counts as if it rests there.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is this? According to רבי עקיבא, who says that an object caught in the air of an area is treated as if it were resting there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks which opinion רב פפא's case fits, and suggests it fits only רבי עקיבא. This sets up the next step, which explains why it would not fit the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For carrying on שבת, a person is liable only when the object 'rests' in the new domain. רבי עקיבא says that once the object is in the air over the courtyard, it already counts as resting there. So for him, the sale and the שבת violation both happen at the same moment, when the animal enters the courtyard's airspace.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Asks whose opinion a statement follows.
Caught. An object held in the airspace of an area.
It is treated as if it were resting there.

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Rabbi Akiva,
who says: an object caught in the air is treated as if it had come to rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion רב פפא's case depends on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does רב פפא's explanation of the ברייתא follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא, who holds that קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא.

steps.title: Why the case would not work for the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the case seems to fit only רבי עקיבא: for the רבנן, the buyer acquires the animal as soon as it reaches the courtyard's airspace, but the thief is liable for שבת only when it lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it followed the רבנן: once the animal reaches the airspace of the buyer's courtyard, he has acquired it, but for שבת the thief is not liable until it reaches the ground!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רב פפא's case must follow רבי עקיבא. It shows that under the רבנן, the sale and the שבת violation happen at two different moments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard acquires for its owner even what is in its airspace, so the sale is done once the animal is over the courtyard. The רבנן hold that an object in the air does not count as resting, so the שבת violation happens only when the animal lands. The sale comes first and the death-penalty act comes later, so the thief should not be exempt from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי עקיבא and hold that an object in the air does not count as resting.
It reaches
He acquired it
With regard to the laws of שבת
The ground

steps.whyThisMatters: The exemption of קים ליה בדרבה מיניה applies only when the money obligation and the death-penalty act happen at the same moment. That is why the timing matters so much here.

phrases.english: For if it is according to the Rabbis,
once it reaches the courtyard of his house, he has acquired it,
but with regard to שבת, he is not liable
until it reaches the ground!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for Step 15's claim that the case follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: That רב פפא's case works only according to רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: Under the רבנן, acquiring through the courtyard's airspace happens before the שבת liability, which starts only when the animal lands. So the two do not happen at the same moment.

steps.title: It works for the רבנן too: the buyer acquires only when the animal lands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case can follow the רבנן as well, if the buyer says he will acquire the animal only once it comes to rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the buyer says: 'Your stolen animal will not be acquired by me until it comes to rest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב פפא's case does not have to follow only רבי עקיבא. The buyer can delay the sale until the animal lands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem for the רבנן was that the sale came before the שבת violation. If the buyer says he will acquire only when the animal rests on the ground, the sale happens exactly when it lands. That is also the moment the thief becomes liable for שבת, so the two happen together and the thief is exempt even according to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It will not be acquired by me
Until it comes to rest (lands on the ground)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's case works for everyone. For רבי עקיבא, the sale and the שבת violation happen together in the air. For the רבנן, they happen together if the buyer says he acquires only when the animal lands. Either way, the thief is exempt from paying four or five times.

phrases.english: It is where he says: "Your stolen animal will not be acquired by me
until it comes to rest."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹמֵר: ״לֹא תִּיקְּנֵי לִי גְּנֵיבוּתָיךְ עַד שֶׁתָּנוּחַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in Step 16 by making the moment of the sale match the moment of the שבת violation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case so that it fits both opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's case works only according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer makes the sale take effect only when the animal lands, so the sale and the שבת violation happen together even according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רבא keeps רמי בר חמא's explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא can still be explained the way רמי בר חמא did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, the ברייתא is like רמי בר חמא explained it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא steps in to defend רמי בר חמא's answer against the attack of the חכמים. He is opening his defense, and the proof comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said the sale through picking a fig on שבת is not a real sale at all. רבא rejects that attack and returns to רמי בר חמא's original case instead of רב פפא's courtyard case.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; we keep the earlier explanation

phrases.english: Rava said:
Actually, it is as Rami bar Chama explained;
phrases.notes: He means the sale happened by picking a fig on שבת, the case the חכמים attacked in step 13.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside רב פפא's case and goes back to defend רמי בר חמא against the attack in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 13 that a sale which no court would enforce is not a sale.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defends the original explanation by rejecting the attack's assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sale that no court would enforce, because the act was a capital crime, means nothing legally.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a deal can still take effect when it is actually carried out, as the next steps will show.

steps.title: The case of a harlot's payment from a capital crime
steps.stepSummary: An אתנן is forbidden even from a capital crime, though no court would force that payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah forbade an אתנן as an offering, even if the man was with his own mother. If she sued him before us in court, would we tell him, 'Get up and pay her'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a parallel case from the laws of קרבנות. He points out that a court would never force this payment, yet the Torah still calls it an אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being with one's mother is a capital crime, so a court would never make him pay what he promised. Yet the Torah forbids the animal as an אתנן even in that case. So a payment can be legally real even when a court would never enforce it.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given to a harlot; the Torah forbids it as a קרבן
Was with his own mother, a crime punished by death
She sued / made a claim
In court

phrases.english: The Torah forbade a harlot's payment as an offering –
and this applies even if he was with his own mother;
and if she sued him before us in court,
would we say to him:
"Get up and give her the payment"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶתְנַן אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה – וַאֲפִילּוּ בָּא עַל אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof behind רבא's defense in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a deal can take effect even when a court would never enforce it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's ban on אתנן, which includes even the payment for being with one's mother.

steps.title: The payment counts once he actually gives it
steps.stepSummary: Even though the court would not force him, once he pays, the animal is an אתנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, even though when she sues him in court we do not tell him 'Go give it to her,' once he does give it to her, it is an אתנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא spells out the lesson of the אתנן case. A court will not force him to pay, but if he pays on his own, the payment really counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא separates two things: whether a court will force the payment, and whether the payment counts once it is made. The court will not force it, but the payment still counts. This is the principle he will apply to the stolen animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
Go give it to her (a court order)
Since

steps.whatToRemember: A court refusing to enforce a deal is not the same as the deal meaning nothing. Once it is carried out, it can still count.

phrases.english: Rather, even though
when she sues him in court –
we do not say to him, "Go give it to her,"

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּכִי יָהֵיב לַהּ – הָוֵי אֶתְנַן;
phrases.english: since when he does give it to her – it is a harlot's payment;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי קָא תָבְעָה לֵיהּ בְּדִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 19 and draws the principle out of it.
steps.raayaObject: A deal counts once it is carried out, even if no court would force it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The אתנן case: no court would order the payment, but once paid it is a real אתנן.

steps.title: Applying the principle to the thief's sale
steps.stepSummary: Here too, the court would not force the thief to hand over the animal. The argument continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, even though in terms of payment, if the buyer sued him in court before us, we would not tell him 'Go pay'...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to apply the אתנן principle back to the thief who sold the animal on שבת. The sentence is not finished here; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא admits the point the חכמים made in step 13: a court would not order the thief to hand over the animal. He is setting up the same move as with אתנן, that the sale still counts once it is actually carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same is true in our case
Regarding payment
Go pay (a court order)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is agreeing that the sale means nothing. He only admits the court would not force it. On the next amud he goes on to show the sale still counts.

phrases.english: Here too,
even though, regarding payment –
if he [the buyer] sued [him] before us in court,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: we would not say to him, "Go pay,"

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְעִנְיַן תַּשְׁלוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the principle from step 20 and begins applying it to the thief's sale from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attack in step 13 that the court would not force the thief to hand over the animal.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case: admits the premise of the attack but limits what follows from it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a court would not force the thief to deliver, the sale is nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court would not force him, but, as with אתנן, the sale can still count once it is carried out (completed on the next amud).
